title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation
abstract: arXiv:2608.13754v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how the system reaches its decisions. Mechanistic interpretability is the obvious source of such evidence, and circuit discovery is its most developed instrument. We ask whether that evidence survives the condition under which it would be relied upon: two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.   We pre-registered a crossed grid of seven analytic axes, every level taken from a published implementation, and mapped each discovered circuit through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement. Across 15,840 pre-registered specifications on GPT-2 small and the indirect object identification task, of which 7,561 produced a claim, the derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs (95% CI 0.725 to 0.738) and the modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. translated_title: 解释多样性：电路级可解释性证据无法经受合理的分析变异
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13754v1 公告类型：新 摘要：欧盟人工智能法案要求高风险系统的提供商提交技术文档，描述系统如何做出决策。机械可解释性是此类证据的明显来源，而电路发现是其最成熟的工具。我们询问这些证据是否能在其被依赖的条件下幸存下来：两位有能力的分析师、同一系统、同一工具、不同的合理设置。我们预先注册了一个跨越七个分析轴的交叉网格，每个层级均取自已发表的实现，并通过确定性声明映射将每个发现的电路映射到结构化的附件IV声明。在GPT-2小模型和间接宾语识别任务上，共15,840个预先注册的规格中，7,561个产生了声明，得出的声明在73.2%的规格对中翻转（95%置信区间0.725至0.738），而众数声明仅占据41.1%的空间。该证据未能通过可行性检验。
tldr: 该论文通过大规模预注册实验表明，电路级可解释性证据在合理的分析设置变化下高度不稳定，无法满足欧盟AI法案对高风险系统技术文档的可靠性要求。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates through large-scale pre-registered experiments that circuit-level interpretability evidence is highly unstable under defensible analytic variations, failing to meet the reliability requirements for EU AI Act technical documentation.
